discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion
motivation: In 2005 two independent analyses, of the SDSS luminous red galaxy sample (led by Eisenstein) and of the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Percival and collaborators), detected the imprint of primordial sound waves in the clustering of galaxies: the baryon acoustic oscillation feature predicted from the coupled photon-baryon plasma of the early universe. This confirmed in the late-time universe the same physics seen in the CMB, and gave cosmology a robust standard ruler whose length is set by well-understood linear physics and is largely immune to astrophysical systematics. Eisenstein's theoretical work made the method precise, including reconstruction techniques, and Percival led its development into a precision tool. BAO is now the backbone of BOSS, eBOSS, DESI and Euclid, and DESI's BAO measurements provide the sharpest current test of whether dark energy is a cosmological constant. Few observational discoveries have so transformed how we test the standard cosmological model.
